title: A Tale of Two Walks: Kipnis, Marchioro and Presutti Meet Kac in a Quantum World
authors: Qian Chen, Jingcheng Liu, Minglong Qin, Leonard Schulman, Fang Song, Penghui Yao, Mingnan Zhao
abstract: We reveal an unexpected connection between the parallel Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. The twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace is exactly encoded by a classical Markov chain on partitions, which lifts to a parallel KMP process on complete graphs. This correspondence reduces the analysis of the twirling channel to the mixing of the parallel KMP process. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in the number of copies $t$.   For the standard KMP process on general graphs, we prove a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture: at fixed accuracy, the mixing time of the $t$-particle process is at most a constant times the single-particle mixing time multiplied by the logarithm of the number of vertices, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the total variation mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde O(n^3)$ (Kook and Vempala, 2026) to $\widetilde O(n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution.   Our main technical contribution is conditional product structure for both parallel and standard KMP processes. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the labeled particles evolve independently. Combining this structure with an exact coupling yields mixing bounds uniform in the number of particles for both unlabeled KMP models. These bounds are sharp up to logarithmic factors and imply rapid convergence of the parallel Kac twirling channel on the symmetric subspace.
summary: This work reveals a fundamental link between the quantum parallel Kac's walk and the classical Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. By showing this equivalence, the authors derive sharp, uniform mixing time bounds for the KMP process, improving known results for random walks on simplices. This advances the understanding of convergence rates in complex interacting particle systems.
main_problem: The paper establishes a deep connection between the parallel Kac's walk (a quantum process) and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process (a classical interacting particle system). It aims to analyze the mixing times of these processes.
main_result: The analysis shows that the quantum twirling channel converges rapidly to the Haar measure, and it proves a mixing time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs.
method: The authors use techniques involving conditional product structure, exact coupling, and relating quantum dynamics to classical Markov chains on partitions to derive sharp mixing bounds.
model_or_system: The models include the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes t}$, the standard KMP process on general graphs, and the coordinate hit-and-run process on the standard simplex.
key_observables: Mixing time, total variation distance, and the rate of convergence to the Haar measure.
important_parameters: Number of copies $t$, dimension $d$, and error tolerance $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the conditional product structure holding for both quantum and classical KMP dynamics.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the equivalence between the parallel Kac's walk and a classical partition resampling chain. It then applies advanced Markov chain techniques to prove the mixing time bounds for this classical process, culminating in applications to specific random walks like coordinate hit-and-run.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum randomizing processes (Kac walk) and classical mixing dynamics (KMP) provides powerful tools for analyzing convergence in complex many-body systems, relevant for understanding thermalization and scrambling in quantum many-body physics.
